content_sections.title: Notice both information needs
content_sections.body_text: Situation card: a visitor needs Gate 4 and must confirm a 5:20 departure. The visitor can ask a friend or an unfamiliar staff member directly. Keep Gate 4 and 5:20 visible. A complete exchange asks about both details and receives both details.

content_sections.title: Match wording to the person
content_sections.body_text: To a friend: ‘Help me find Gate 4 and check 5:20, please.’ To staff: ‘Excuse me. Can you help me find Gate 4 and confirm the 5:20 departure, please?’ Excuse me comes first to get an unfamiliar listener’s attention; the fuller request states both needs.

content_sections.title: Model and rehearse the exchange
content_sections.body_text: Visitor: ‘Excuse me. Can you help me find Gate 4 and confirm the 5:20 departure, please?’ Staff: ‘Yes. Gate 4 is on the left, and your departure is at 5:20.’ Visitor: ‘Thank you.’ Point to each requested detail and its matching answer, then rehearse both roles.

content_sections.title: Mark word stress and self-check
content_sections.body_text: STA-tion /ˈsteɪ.ʃən/ has two syllables; the first has the main stress. Keep /eɪ/ full and make STA a little longer and stronger; make /ʃən/ lighter. Say the word alone, then in the staff exchange. Check: Excuse me comes first, Gate 4 and 5:20 are both answered, and stress stays on the first syllable.
